title: Understanding the Elbow Method
text: The elbow method is a technique used to determine the optimal number of clusters (k) in k-Means clustering. It involves plotting the sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned cluster center as a function of the number of clusters.

title: Interpreting the Elbow Plot
text: In the elbow plot, the x-axis represents the number of clusters (k), and the y-axis represents the sum of squared distances. The 'elbow' point is where the rate of decrease sharply changes, indicating the optimal k.

title: Evaluating Clustering Outcomes
text: When evaluating clustering outcomes, consider both the compactness of clusters and the separation between them. Compact clusters have points close to their center, while well-separated clusters have distinct boundaries.
